newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index trading returns to normal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index trading returns to normal.

text.p: Trading in stock index options returned to relative calm Monday after Friday's frenzied action that began with a delayed opening.
Traders said volume slackened but steady activity was seen in both puts and calls.
"Volatility's coming in, the market's going up, but there's not much business and no volume," said one S&P 100 stock index trader at the CBOE.
The OEX was up 2.94 points at 720.27 by 1100 CST/1700 GMT, off its 722.22 session peak.
"We're not seeing much OEX business," said Hank Nothnagel, senior vice president of options trading at EVEREN Securities.
He said investors still appeared bullish, at least on technology shares, despite last week's shakeout.
On Friday, stocks fell sharply off the opening bell after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan warned in a speech Thursday night about "irrational exuberance" in financial markets.
But they rebounded solidly, with the Dow industrial average ending down about 55 points after having fallen as much as 144.
The technology-heavy Nasdaq composite index fell 41 points intraday but closed down only 12.
Stocks continued their recovery Monday, with the Dow ahead 35 points at 6,417 and the Nasdaq up 16 at about 1,304.
"With the market up pretty good this morning, call options lost quite a bit of air," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in the OEX at the CBOE.
He said investors were selling still-high call premiums "and that's where the opportunity is versus buying puts."
The at-the-money December 720 OEX call was trading at 10, with a bid/ask of 9-7/8/10.
The December 720 put was trading at 7-3/8, with a bid/ask of 7/7-1/4.
Callahan said put buyers were very active during Friday morning's selloff but not too many options participants appeared to be caught off guard.
In the OEX Monday, the December 725 call, trading up 1/2 at 6-3/4, and the December 720 put were the two most active, with 6,840 and 6,920 contracts changing hands, respectively.
Among S&P 500 index options, most activity was seen in out-of-the-money calls, but the most volume was in the January 730 and 745 puts.
